why: Quote confirmed VERBATIM at code-review.md:285, and the whole line was read: the second sentence ('It reports correctness bugs and reuse, simplification, and efficiency cleanups.') reinforces rather than reverses it. The claimed behaviour is fully supported one layer down the same page: :295 'To review something else, pass a target: a file path, a PR number, a branch name, or a ref range'; :299-:300 '--fix: applies the findings to your working tree after the review' / '--comment: posts the findings as inline PR comments'; :320 'Pass an effort level ... Without an effort argument, the review uses the session's current effort'; :339 confirms it is a skill ('/code-review is marked disable-model-invocation'). NOT a subscription-gated surface either: :10 says explicitly that on plans without the GitHub App 'you can still review a diff locally with the /code-review command', so this is not one of the fork's deliberately dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, and it is not a rebranding difference. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) nor of its four false-positive shapes. Repo side confirmed with -a greps: find over the whole tree returns SKILL.md only under apps/electron/resources/skills/{plugin-creator,skill-creator} (plus the dist copy of the same two and plugin test fixtures); getBundledAssetsDir (packages/shared/src/utils/paths.ts:218-228) resolves the bundle from exactly that resources/skills root, so there is no second bundled-skill source; seed.ts:31-49 is verbatim as cited ('the bundle itself is the only authority on which slugs are bundled'). There is no built-in slash-command registry supplying /code-review either, and no bundled workflow (packages/shared/src/workflows holds only the keyword/consent/loader modules). So the gap is real and the row survives. ONE CLAUSE OF THE OUR-STATE IS WRONG and is corrected below: 'the ReportFindings tool therefore ships with no in-product caller' does not hold. The tool ships (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1048, safeMode allow, readOnly) and IS deliberately wired to an in-product review producer: BUILTIN_AGENT_DEFINITIONS ships a `reviewer` agent whose system prompt is 'You are a reviewer agent. Focus on defects and test gaps. Return findings first, with file references, and avoid rewriting code.' (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:186-193), and packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:83 puts ReportFindings in SUBAGENT_ALWAYS_AVAILABLE_TOOLS precisely so that agent can reach it, with the reason spelled out at :70-82 ('the tool exists so a REVIEW agent can hand back structured findings ... unreachable from the exact agent the contract was written for'). This is the audit history's 'consequence is false because something upstream already handled it' shape, caught one layer up. What is genuinely missing is the user-invocable /code-review entry point with its documented scope (branch commits ahead of upstream plus uncommitted changes), its --fix/--comment flags, its effort/target argument grammar, its background-subagent default with the documented foreground fallbacks, and disable-model-invocation.
correctedState: No `/code-review` bundled skill ships (nor `/simplify`, `/verify`, `/run`, `/loop`): `apps/electron/resources/skills/` contains exactly two, `plugin-creator` and `skill-creator`, and `getBundledAssetsDir` (packages/shared/src/utils/paths.ts:218) resolves the bundle from that single root, so there is no other source. There is no built-in slash-command registry entry and no bundled workflow for review either, so the diff-review entry point and its whole argument grammar (`--fix`, `--comment`, effort level, target, background-subagent default, `disable-model-invocation`) are absent. But `ReportFindings` is NOT an orphan: it ships at packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1048 and is deliberately granted to the bundled `reviewer` subagent — whose prompt is 'Return findings first, with file references' (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:186-193) — via SUBAGENT_ALWAYS_AVAILABLE_TOOLS at packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:83, whose docblock at :70-82 names that agent as the reason the tool exists. The gap is the user-facing command, not the tool's reachability.
